correctness.rationale: The block operator is explicitly surjective and has one-dimensional kernel in the orthogonal complement of R(K). It commutes with K=P_R(K), preserves R(K)-perp, and fixes the singleton Parseval K-frame. Hence all three excesses are exactly zero while U is not injective. The restricted-injectivity repair follows from a self-contained exact sequence of synthesis kernels for an onto operator on the projected frame space.

evidence: Corollary 5.11 states global injectivity of U as the necessary and sufficient condition for equality of the three excesses.
For a frame with synthesis operator T and an onto operator V, the transformed synthesis operator is VT, so excess equality is a statement about the relation between ker(T) and ker(VT).
The exact sequence from ker(T) to ker(VT) to ker(V) makes the finite-excess obstruction equivalent to injectivity of V.

originality.rationale: Exact-source and semantic searches covered Corollary 5.11, excess preservation under onto operators, synthesis-kernel formulations, restriction to R(K), and errata. A published prior result already shows that projection can overcount K-frame excess for arbitrary K-frames; the accepted claim is logically distinct because its atom is already in R(K), where projection does nothing, and it targets the global-injectivity conclusion.
residual_risks: A nonindexed erratum, thesis remark, or informal note may already contain the restricted-injectivity correction.

A separate published objection to the source's general projected-excess identity remains outside this claim; the present witness was chosen specifically so that projection is the identity on every atom.

value.rationale: Corollary 5.11 advertises a necessary and sufficient condition connecting K-frame excess to invertibility properties of an operator. The counterexample shows that excess confined to R(K) cannot determine global injectivity, even in the cleanest possible Parseval, zero-excess case. The repair identifies the correct visible operator U|R(K) and gives an exact finite-excess kernel formula.
